concept_overview: Build a clean internal support operations app for a helpdesk lead. The app tracks support tickets, reviews queue health, and lets operators update ticket status without external integrations.

primary_jobs: open a ticket and update its status

frontend_design_document: Persistent UI should be sparse and scan-first. Use one page title, one short subtitle, a compact ticket list, and clear row actions. Do not create generic dashboard panels, decorative feeds, or repeated KPI cards.
ui_design_document:
Pages:
- Tickets: PageHeader + ResourceTable. Columns: ticket, priority, status, updated, action. Include search and filters.
- Queue Settings: PageHeader + Form for default assignment queue and SLA threshold.
Use ResourceTable for collection pages and Form for settings. Use SummaryStrip only if it materially helps scanning.
experience_spec_document: The app has durable pages for /tickets and /settings. /tickets is the landing page. The UI is declarative_page by default. No route needs custom_react_page.

app_build_plan.agent_message: Use the seeded Support Operations scope and generate deterministic app artifacts through explicit task batches.
app_build_plan.theme_preferences: Dark, sparse, scan-first support operations UI using the captured typography.

build_tasks.description: Generate the tickets module YAML contract.
build_tasks.initial_message: Generate only YAML code_files for the tickets module contract. Do not call generate_scaffold and do not emit backend Python. Actions: list_tickets, get_ticket, update_status, save_settings. For generated modules, every action handler_method must exactly equal the action id, so update_status must use handler_method: update_status. Events: domain.tickets.status_updated. Settings: default_queue and sla_hours. Admin panel: support page ResourceTable bound to list_tickets with update_status as a row action. Declare python_stubs for backend/handler.py, backend/service.py, backend/repo.py, backend/policy.py, and backend/schemas.py.
acceptance_criteria: module.yaml declares ticket list, get, update_status, and save_settings actions
python_stubs declares handler.py, service.py, repo.py, policy.py, and schemas.py

build_tasks.description: Generate the tickets module handler, service, repo, and policy layers.
build_tasks.initial_message: Generate only modules/tickets/backend/handler.py, service.py, repo.py, and policy.py. Read dependency_task_outputs for task_tickets_contract, task_tickets_models, and task_data_contract before emitting code. module.handler is backend.handler:TicketsModule; handler.py must define class TicketsModule exactly and implement every module.yaml handler_method exactly: list_tickets, get_ticket, update_status, save_settings. Runtime calls handler methods as method(ctx, **params), so context must be the first parameter after self. service.py must implement the same four service methods and must consume request fields directly from **params using module.yaml input fields; do not use params.get("payload") unless payload is a declared input field. save_settings must read default_queue and sla_hours directly from params; do not invent params["settings"]. repo.py must provide the required persistence operations using context.persistence.collection("tickets", "tickets"), and service.py must publish domain.tickets.status_updated when update_status commits. Do not emit pass statements, TODOs, or placeholder implementation comments; return concrete repo-backed results or explicit empty/acknowledgement values.
acceptance_criteria: handler.py defines TicketsModule and implements list_tickets, get_ticket, update_status, and save_settings
handler methods accept ctx as the first parameter after self and delegate to service.py
service.py publishes declared domain events after mutation
